By Charlotte Goldstone
20 November 2026
The anticipated recovery in global airfreight capacity next year may prove less substantial than headline growth forecasts suggest.
Two aviation consultancies are warning that much of the increase will constitute restoration of capacity lost during the Gulf conflict, rather than new supply.
Aevean forecasts international capacity growth of 6% to 7% next year, against demand growth of 5%-6%; Rotate expects capacity to increase 5% to -6%, compared with demand growth of 4%-5%.
Maarten Wormer, head of consulting at Aevean, told The Loadstar the apparent improvement in supply could be misleading.
“That capacity figure flatters the picture, because most of it is the conflict-hit base recovering, not new supply,” he said.
Measured against 2025, Aevean expects demand to have grown around 10% by 2027, compared with capacity growth of 9%.
“The market therefore ends 2027 slightly tighter than before the conflict, not looser,” Mr Wormer predicted.
He said combined capacity out of Doha, Dubai, and Abu Dhabi remained around 12% below pre-conflict levels, equivalent to approximately 2,200 tonnes a day.
However, Gulf carriers Emirates, Qatar Airways, and Etihad were already operating at or above 2025 levels, with the shortfall almost entirely attributable to foreign freighter operators, whose capacity at the three hubs was down 49%.
“If they do come back, they will mostly move freighters from other lanes rather than add new supply to the global market,” he said.
Tim van Leeuwen, VP and head of consulting at Rotate, agreed that the return of Gulf capacity was unlikely to have a substantial additional impact.
“What is missing are mostly non-Gulf carriers operating to the region, but that missing capacity has been deployed elsewhere,” he told The Loadstar .
He said the consultant expected slightly weaker market conditions for airlines next year, although fuel-price uncertainty made rate predictions difficult.
Both consultancies expect considerable regional differences, with Asia-North America remaining constrained while Asia-Europe faces weaker demand and potentially excess capacity.
Aevean said Asia-North America air trade grew 24% in September and it expects demand on the corridor to increase by at least 10% in 2027. By contrast, Asia-Europe air trade fell 15% in September following the introduction of the EU’s €3 parcel duty, with ecommerce volumes down 40%, despite general cargo growing 7%.
Mr Wormer warned that returning Gulf capacity would be concentrated on the Asia-Europe corridor, potentially exacerbating the imbalance.
Rotate is already observing airlines shifting capacity from Asia-Europe towards Asia and North America in response to the weaker ecommerce demand.
Mr van Leeuwen said the Transpacific continued to face the greatest supply-demand pressure, with China-origin capacity particularly constrained and some US-bound cargo moving via Europe.
Siddhant Iyer, head of cargo global partnerships and customer solutions at Cathay Cargo, also highlighted pressure on available space, with more customers turning to its Cathay Priority product to secure capacity on busy flights.
He said demand for specialist handling, including out-of-gauge server rack shipments, was increasing, while tonnage across Cathay’s special shipment solutions had risen 17% year on year.
Meanwhile, Mr Wormer warned that AI-financing conditions and further export controls could alter the trajectory of technology-related cargo demand.
Another risk lies in the ageing aircraft fleet. Aevean estimates that around 1,600 freighters and widebody passenger aircraft are beyond typical retirement age, approximately 6.5 times average annual retirements.
“If fuel stays high or demand softens, those aircraft are the first to be parked, and supply can fall faster than models assume,” Mr Wormer warned.
The consultant expects demand growth to begin outpacing capacity again in 2028, potentially tightening the market through to the end of the decade.

Volkswagen ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept Packs 362 Ponies, Looks Great But Does It Have a Soul?
10 photos
Photo: Volkswagen
The German automaker Volkswagen is busy churning out one novelty after another, and all types of powertrains are included - as well as a fresh concept vehicle, the VW ID. Polo GTI Clubsport.
Over in North America, Volkswagen is attending the 2026 LA Auto Show in Los Angeles, California, which runs through November 29, and proposes there an ensemble of the all-new Atlas and Atlas Cross Sport mid-size crossover SUVs along with a limited edition dedicated to the United States, the Volkswagen Golf GTI Rabbit Edition .
At home on the Old Continent, VW just announced the second-generation T-Roc R high-performance subcompact crossover SUV with 328 hp and a higher price than its Golf R cousin, and already they’re off to EV shenanigans, too. It’s all thanks to the new Volkswagen ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept, of course.
The prototype gets the Clubsport series into the zero-emissions world, packing motorsport-inspired elements along with 270 kW (367 ps or 362 hp) and a sprint to 100 kph or 62 mph in 4.7 seconds, plus a top speed of 240 kph or 149 mph.
With a new ceramic brake system behind the cool black and red alloy wheels, the concept sees the racetrack as part of its duties, and it’s also packing just two side doors unlike the ID. Polo and ID. Polo GTI warrants its exclusivity and the fact that it “builds on 50 years of GTI success with an innovative technology concept and classic Volkswagen design .”
It still uses regular components, though – the MEB+ platform with front-wheel drive and the latest APP550 electric motor – but marks the 50th anniversary of the GTI label by also joining electric mobility with the sporty nameplate.
The concept car will be shown to the public next week at the Essen Motor Show, November 27 through December 6, and also comes with a contemporary widebody style plus a large front splitter, diffuser, and rear wing. It’s based on the VW ID. Polo GTI with 166 kW or 226 ps and 222 hp, and thus keeps the FWD setup.
There’s also an electronic front differential lock, a 52 kWh high-voltage battery that can actually provide up to 290 kW for short bursts, and DCC (adaptive chassis control) tuned for use on circuits, along with the new ceramic brakes of the one-box brake system.
The exterior has 50-mm flared wings, but the most striking feature is that there are only two doors and also just two seats inside – the driver and front passenger sit on Recaro racing bucket seats with red five-point harnesses; there is no infotainment system, and the rear and luggage compartment have been cleared to make way for a rollover bar painted in the GTI Tornado red color.
One last detail – Volkswagen trainees handled the dark ArtVelours microfibre fabric with red topstitching used on the dash panel, side trims, and in many other places. The ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept got the high-torque APP550 motor from the rear unit of larger models like the ID. Tiguan and ID. 7, and now the torque rating has jumped from 290 to 550 Nm (214 to 406 lb-ft).
Volkswagen has marked the 50th anniversary of the GTI sub-brand with four new models this year: the Golf GTI Edition, the electric ID.3 GTI and ID. Polo GTI, and now also the fancy ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept. As always with these zero-emission models that try to act sporty, though, we have to wonder – do they have a soul? 2028 BMW i3 Touring Spied With Roof-Mounted Emergency Lights
17 photos
Photo: SH Proshots
The electric brother of the 3 Series Touring has picked up an interesting accessory. The latest prototype of the i3 Touring carries emergency vehicle lighting on its roof, something the carparazzi haven't encountered on previous test vehicles of the NA1. Obviously enough, those lights are there because the automaker is developing a new member of the BMW Authority Vehicles family.
Before going any further, BMW Authority Vehicles come in many shapes and sizes. From the 1 Series all the way to the 7 Series and X7, these purpose-built machines are modified by the German manufacturer for government agencies, customs, medical, fire, and police duties. A white-painted prototype with blue roof lighting, meanwhile, suggests emergency services and police homologation.
The combination of a longroof with fleet-vehicle white paint and blue lights, on the other hand, suggests operational roles. Think rapid-response vehicle or highway patrol vehicle. It's also worth mentioning that BMW has a thing for equipping pre-production or early-build vehicles like this for internal emergency response at its production facilities, including Munich and Dingolfing.
Beyond the roof-mounted light bar, this prototype does not show any other modification. Camouflaged like there's no tomorrow out back and up front, the i3 Touring wears aero-conscious black machined wheels that frame silver brake calipers. As such, the prototype clearly isn't based on the M Performance model that is expected to be called M60 xDrive.
The rest of the lineup should comprise the 50 xDrive, 40 xDrive, and the rear-wheel-drive 30, with production scheduled to start in July 2027. Based on this information, the i3 Touring is a 2028 model by US automotive standards. Whether the i3 Touring is coming to the United States, we do not know for certain.
Photo: SH Proshots Back in June 2026, the North American vice prez of product management acknowledged that the M5 Touring outsells the sedan, making a case for more exciting wagons in the United States of America. While there may be momentum in the market, with customers also petitioning for the M3 Touring, an electric wagon is very different from one powered by a singing inline-six engine.
The wheels in question, which form a five-pointed star with their spokes, are standard in Germany on the 40 xDrive and 50 xDrive versions of the sedan. Unfortunately, the camouflage makes it impossible to determine the visual package that BMW specified for this prototype. Nevertheless, the longroof in question has the same proportions teased by its maker back in March 2026.
Two months later, back in May 2026, former chief executive officer Oliver Zipse shared even more teaser images of the i3 Touring. He also stated the 3 Series Touring is very popular with business customers and families, hence BMW's decision to add the i3 Touring to the 3er's range. Just like the sedan, the roomier specification will be assembled at BMW Group Plant Munich in Germany.
Because of the wheels, it's natural to assume that BMW is testing either the 40 xDrive or the punchier 50 xDrive here. The lesser dual-motor powertrain is listed with 275 kW (369 hp) and 520 Nm (384 lb-ft) on tap, along with a driving range of up to 710 kilometers (441 miles) on a full charge of its 82.8-kWh battery.
Stepping up to the 50 xDrive means 345 kW (463 hp) and 645 Nm (476 lb-ft) in optimal conditions, along with no more than 912 kilometers (567 miles) from 108.7 kilowatt-hours. Being a wagon, the i3 Touring 50 xDrive should be heavier than its four-door brother, whose 0-60 estimate in the US is 4.5 seconds. Even if it would need 4.6 seconds to hit 60 mph (97 kph), that's plenty quick for a family hauler, police, or rapid-response vehicle.

Australia's Hyundai Sonata Gets Discontinued, New i30 Sedan Hybrid Taking Over in 2027
49 photos
Photo: Hyundai
Can you believe Hyundai Australia dealers couldn't sell more than 8 examples of the Sonata in October 2026? That figure says more than enough about the South Korean model's predicament, especially when you find out that Toyota Australia dealers moved 930 units of the hybrid-only Camry during the same month.
Speaking of which, the Sonata's problem gets a lot more serious when you search for the year-to-date registration data. Precisely 187 units were moved through October 2026, resulting in a very disappointing monthly average. Hyundai Australia has now confirmed that Sonata production for Down Under came to a screeching halt in October 2026, ending a run that began in 1989.
More than 73,000 units were sold thus far, and between you and me, that's a pitiful tally for a model competing in such a mainstream segment. According to WhichCar?, which cites Hyundai Australia’s Guido Schenken, the midsizer won't get a direct successor in this part of the world. The CN8-generation i30 Sedan Hybrid will take its place, a.k.a. the redesigned Elantra Hybrid.
Revealed in June at the Busan Motor Show, the CN8 is called Avante back home and is larger in every respect compared to the preceding Elantra. According to Hyundai Motor America's tech specs, the new compact is leaning into the mid-size segment, being 3.4 inches longer and 1.2 inches wider. These dimensions make it a pretty good indirect successor to the Sonata N Line in Australia.
It's also taller, but curiously enough, its drag coefficient is better. The drag coefficient figure is all the more interesting once you take in the low-poly design language, which includes flared fenders by default. Returning to a classic three-box profile with a flat roofline, the 2027 model can be described as both sharp and industrial. The interior, meanwhile, is on the minimalist side.
Photo: Hyundai Back in Australia, the current-gen Sonata rolled out in 2021. A facelift arrived in the latter part of 2023, bringing a full-width front lighting signature, a far more angular front bumper, a revised dashboard, and extra tech. From a mechanical standpoint, it's a solid car that offers plenty of muscle as well, courtesy of a 2.5-liter turbo inline-four mill that is joined by a wet-clutch DCT.
The N Line is most definitely a looker, but as with every N Line specification, it's mostly show rather than extra driving excitement. While it may look considerably more ambitious than the Toyota Camry, the people have voted with their wallets in favor of the far more boring and way more frugal alternative.
Hyundai Australia's best year for the Sonata was 1997, when 7,390 units found buyers. For a brief period, it wasn't even called Sonata. The i45 nonsense stopped in early 2013, and the Sonata nameplate returned for 2015 with the seventh generation. The year-to-date sales recorded through October 2026 put the Sonata behind some of the brand's electric vehicles, including the Ioniq 6.
The Camry recorded 10,401 deliveries in the first ten months of the current year, up 22.2 percent from the same period last year. Adding insult to injury, the Sonata N Line costs more than the top-of-the-range Camry SL grade as of this writing.

Searching suspected explosive ground puts people in danger. Skylark Labs has demonstrated a humanoid that can take on that search with a standard handheld metal detector—sweeping the ground and responding to its alert under human supervision. The aim is to keep explosive ordnance disposal (EOD) specialists farther from suspected hazards while they direct and assess the search.
In an experiment conducted for an EOD supplier, the robot picked up the detector, swept a designated search area and stopped and backed off when it sounded. It carried out the sequence without a separate command for each step.
Skylark says visual and audio feedback guided the robot through the task. The detector’s beep became an input to its next action, connecting what the machine sensed with what it did. Company footage shows the humanoid sweeping outdoors alongside a person performing the same search. The demo footage can be seen here.
“Our customers already own and trust their detectors. A robot that learns the search from the specialists who do it, and then runs it with that same equipment, takes people out of the most dangerous moments without handing them more work.”
EOD supplier representative
The threat is persistent. Action on Armed Violence recorded 10,376 IED incidents across 94 countries between 2015 and 2024, causing 83,529 civilian deaths and injuries. Suspected devices can also halt movement, restrict access and divert personnel.
EOD teams already rely on robots. In 2022, the U.S. Air Force began fielding 170 L3Harris T7 systems : tracked machines controlled by an operator. Skylark is pursuing a humanoid that carries out an assigned search without requiring a person to direct each movement.
The humanoid form is central to that approach. Its hands, reach and posture let it work with equipment designed for people, including the detectors EOD teams already carry. Learning to use those tools reduces the need to redesign equipment around a robot. The intended payoff is practical: less time spent directing a machine, and less human exposure at the front of the search.
Skylark’s Continual Field-Adaptive Models , or CFAMs, provide the learning capability. Specialists demonstrate how to handle familiar equipment and carry out a search. Skylark says the detector-search skill was taught through a few minutes of human demonstration. The models are designed to keep adapting on the device as the robot works, without a separate retraining cycle.
CFAM delivered about 30% higher task success than a standard model in a real-world manipulation test. In a separate evaluation, it matched a standard model’s performance using just 40% of the training data. It also learned new skills with little loss of earlier capabilities. Performance in new search conditions is still being tested.
“The first footsteps onto unswept ground carry the greatest risk. If a machine can reduce human risk while discerning the unknown, specialized judgment is reserved for the most complex challenges. That only works if we can readily summon machine sensing and human judgment for combined understanding that neither system can achieve alone.”
Retired U.S. Marine Corps Lt. Gen. Michael S. Groen , former director of the Pentagon’s Joint Artificial Intelligence Center and a member of Skylark Labs’ Defense Advisory Board
The demonstrated work is detection support. Physical handling and disposal remain development goals. The humanoid’s value will depend on carrying out a defined search reliably enough that a specialist can supervise from greater separation, instead of being the first person onto unswept ground.
“Our mission is to enable machines—including humanoids—to independently carry out explosive ordnance disposal tasks, keeping people away from potentially lethal threats. We’re building the AI brain that allows these machines to learn efficiently and adapt to unfamiliar objects, terrain, and changing conditions, with the goal of making them reliable and effective in complex EOD operations,” said Amarjot Singh, Founder and CEO of Skylark Labs.
Skylark’s longer-term goal is a team of humanoids working together. Hive, its framework for coordinating multiple machines, is already deployed in oil and gas operations in the United States, India and the Middle East. Applied to EOD, it could let robots divide a search area, share findings and hand off work as conditions change, with one specialist overseeing the team.
The goal is to send the machine first, while keeping the specialist in charge.

Savini Wheels Launches New Forged Design Called 'Fluted' and Maybach and GTA Play Perfectly Together

Photo: Savini Wheels / Instagram
This week has been filled with tributes for the latest installment in the Grand Theft Auto video game series, and Savini Wheels didn’t miss the chance to associate with the high-profile franchise for its latest release – even if only unofficially.
First and foremost – let’s talk about the company a little. Savini Wheels was founded in California in 2003 and is a specialist in custom forged and flow-formed wheels for luxury models. Basically, it’s a direct competitor to another well-known name in the space of made-to-order, custom-forged wheels for luxury sedans, exotic sports cars, and high-end SUVs – Forgiato Designs - and they were both established in the Los Angeles area in the early 2000s.
Alas, while Forgiato is geared toward flashy and oversized models that attract a certain crowd, Savini Wheels used to be attracted more to the slightly more affordable space or the performance side of the concave wheel business. Well, now the boundaries have blurred.
And it’s all thanks to Savini’s latest release – the monoblock forged ‘Fluted’ design that can be finished in any custom build or specification and can be drilled to the customer’s exact bolt pattern. Savini says it belongs to the SL series, which is “made for the world's most exclusive vehicles, providing function and style without having to replace the luxurious center cap for such vehicles, including Rolls-Royce” models.
It’s also available in a DuoBlock configuration, and to showcase it on an actual vehicle, Savini used a flashy Mercedes-Maybach GLS to present it to the world. The combination is quite extreme, as the Maybach is also custom – done in a single monochromatic paint or wrap and tucked a bit lower on the new Fluted model – which is available in 20-, 22-, 24-, and 26-inch configurations. We bet that the latter is also used here in these eloquent pictures.
Naturally, Savini found a Grand Theft Auto VI mural somewhere around town to showcase the Maybach and their Fluted model, which certainly isn’t a bad idea since a lot of aftermarket outlets have spent a bit of time with their built cars and GTA VI-related activities. U.S. rail traffic rose 7.3% in the week ending November 14, 2026, compared with the same week last year, as double-digit intermodal growth outpaced gains in conventional carload shipments, according to the Association of American Railroads .
Intermodal volume increased 10.7% year over year, while total carloads rose 3.3%, AAR said in a weekly update. Eight of the 10 carload commodity groups recorded gains.
(Chart: AAR)
Motor vehicles and parts posted the strongest percentage increase among carload categories, rising 16.2%. Forest products followed with a 14% gain, while metallic ores and metals increased 10.7% and petroleum and petroleum products advanced 10.3%.
The remaining categories posting increases were farm products excluding grain, and food, up 3.1%; chemicals, up 2.3%; nonmetallic minerals, up 2.1%; and coal, up 0.9%. Grain shipments fell 4.7%.
Year-to-date traffic advances 4%
Through the first 45 weeks of 2026, total U.S. rail traffic increased 4% compared with the corresponding period in 2025. Intermodal volume rose 5%, while carload traffic gained 2.7%.
Grain remained the strongest year-to-date carload category, up 9.4%, despite its weekly decline. Metallic ores and metals increased 8.8%, and petroleum and petroleum products rose 7.8%. Coal was the only carload category below its year-earlier level for the year to date, down 1.5%.
North American rail traffic also rises
Across nine reporting U.S., Canadian and Mexican railroads, combined weekly traffic increased 7.2% year over year. North American carloads rose 3.7%, while intermodal volume climbed 10.5%. Total traffic for the first 45 weeks of the year increased 3.5%.
Why it matters: The results show rail traffic growth extending across most major commodity groups, while forest products and automotive bucked high interest rates that have held down home construction and car sales for much of the year.
